text:
From the second period on, Edmonton drove more of the play. It didn't matter. Vegas scored three times in that stretch, Trevor Connelly finished with two goals and an assist, and the Golden Knights left Rogers Place with a 5-3 win that stretched the Oilers' slide to four games without a win (0-3-1).

The start belonged to Vegas. Jack Eichel scored on the power play at 6:13 of the first, set up by Mitch Marner and Victor Olofsson, and Connelly followed less than three minutes later with a backhand. Edmonton barely touched the puck in dangerous places: Vegas out-chanced them 0.75 to 0.06 in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the first period. The Oilers answered in the second. Colton Dach tipped one in early, and with 19 seconds left in the period Connor McDavid tied it, a goal that moved Edmonton's win chance from 28% to 52%.

Then the third got away from them. Nic Dowd scored 2:08 in, the biggest swing of the night (48% to 74%), and Eichel made it 4-2 at 5:29. Vasily Podkolzin pulled one back 16 seconds later, and Edmonton kept coming. Carter Hart's biggest save came on Ryan Nugent-Hopkins late in the third, and Connelly sealed it at 17:28. Connelly, the 19th pick in 2024, had five shots and 0.99 expected goals on his own.

The uncomfortable part for Edmonton is that the process wasn't the problem. The Oilers had more shot attempts (59 to 50), more even-strength expected goals (2.82 to 2.17), and in our replays of every shot they win this game 58% of the time. What they didn't get was a save: Devon Levi allowed 1.3 more goals than his 26 shots deserved, while Hart was about even. Four games without a win is the kind of stretch that starts conversations about a goalie, and this one will.

For Vegas, days after Mark Stone became the franchise's career points leader, others carried it. Eichel added 0.31 wins with his two goals, the most of anyone, and Connelly looked at home in one of the loudest rivalries in the West.
headline: Connelly and Eichel push the Oilers to four without a win
